title: Windows drive-relative and state-directory paths pass attempt-path validation
reasoning: PureWindowsPath("C:outside") is drive-qualified but not absolute, so it passes. Likewise, ".clawpatch\\state" is recognized as Windows path components but evades the literal forward-slash .clawpatch checks. These inputs defeat the validator's stated outside/state-only path restrictions on Windows.
reproduction: Call the validator with ["C:outside"] or [".clawpatch\\state"]; neither satisfies any rejection condition.
recommendation: Reject any Windows path with a drive, and compare normalized PurePosixPath/PureWindowsPath components so a first component of .clawpatch is rejected for either separator style.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No included tests cover _impl_validate_attempt_paths_syntax or Windows-specific unsafe forms.
suggestedRegressionTest: Test drive-relative paths, UNC/device paths, and .clawpatch paths using both slash styles.
minimumFixScope: Harden _impl_validate_attempt_paths_syntax and add cross-platform path-table tests.

history.reasoning: The evidence still exists but moved to validation.py:401-426. The validator now rejects any PureWindowsPath with a drive and rejects .clawpatch as the normalized first Windows component, covering C:outside, UNC/device paths, and both slash styles. Regression tests exist in tests/test_release.py:75-92. The linked attempt's ruff/pytest commands failed only because those executables were unavailable (exit 127), so they provided no validation; fresh targeted validation using the repository's supported unittest command passed both tests. Commit bb42b83 contains the matching source and regression-test repair.
